definition: In this historical heredity usage, midparent means an averaged or mean parent formed from the two parents for studying how ancestry contributes to an offspring. The passage treats it as the starting point for broader averages of ancestors in later generations.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Galton's; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports a historical ‘midparent’ concept and later a generalized ‘mid-s-th parent’ as a mean of ancestry, but it does not explicitly define midparent as an averaged parent formed from exactly two parents.

The added gloss about ‘studying how ancestry contributes to an offspring’ is a broader interpretation of the surrounding heredity theory rather than a statement supported directly by the supplied text.

The packet does not explicitly define “midparent” as “an averaged or mean parent formed from the two parents.” It only says the passage is “modifying Mr. Galton’s definition of midparent” and then describes “a sort of mean of the ancestry in the s th generation,” which is not the same wording or sense as averaging two parents into a midparent.
